findings.text: Slow insertion offers a blocking style entry that keeps retrying the inner try step while a transient contention signal is reported, returning the final object reference or error indication once stable.

Key successor lookup returns the object holding the next distinct key after a given predecessor by scanning the current table and any successor tables linked during resize, reporting unsupported mode for list variant, missing predecessor, or end of data.
Walker registration initializes position state to the start of the table and links the walker into the active table roster, while deregistration removes that linkage.

Walk session start acquires read side protection and validates or reinitializes saved position, requesting a restart when the table reference changed, and walk session stop releases protection while rejoining the roster unless the table is being reclaimed.

Walk iteration advances across entries within a slot and then across slots and successor tables, with one variant consuming the entry and another observing the current entry without advancing past it.

Table initialization validates hash and comparison configuration, prepares synchronization primitives, normalizes size bounds, selects a default hash routine, allocates the first bucket array with a minimal fallback, publishes it, and arms deferred maintenance work; list variant additionally enables list mode.

Nested bucket access resolves a hash to a bucket reference through layered tables, returning a shared empty marker when no leaf exists, with a separate inserting variant that creates missing intermediate layers.

Scalable bitmap setup creates per word state and optional per cpu allocation hints for a given depth and granularity, resizing refreshes deferred state before adjusting depth, allocation returns a free index or a failure marker, and queue wrappers add wait infrastructure and wake tuning.
Bitmap introspection reports whether any bit is active, counts active and deferred entries, and formats summary counters plus a compact hexadecimal image of live bits for diagnostic output.

Element accounting increments only when insertion truly adds a new member, conflict without table growth preserves the existing object, load beyond about three quarters schedules background maintenance, and persistent contention falls back to a rehash attempt.

Successor search hashes the predecessor key, compares each candidate with a caller supplied comparator when present else a default key comparison, skips the run equal to the predecessor, and returns the first later distinct entry or the first entry of a later bucket.

Initial capacity derives from an element hint inflated by four thirds to allow headroom and rounded up, bounded below by configured minimum and built in defaults, with maximum element count capped to avoid counter overflow and adjusted from a rounded down maximum size.
Default hashing uses a general routine, switching to a word oriented variant with length expressed in words when key length aligns to word size.

Nested lookup consumes low hash bits for the top level then successive page sized chunks while the remaining range stays large, following protected references at each step and yielding no leaf when any level is absent.

Bitmap geometry keeps word count as depth divided by bits per word rounded up, with bits per word as a power of two limited to machine word width, zero depth meaning no storage, and shallow queries scaling each word share proportionally with remainder handling.

Allocation hints start randomized per execution context unless round robin is requested, are repaired when outside current depth, advance past the consumed index when the hint was used, and reset when the map is full.

Deferred clearing either signals whether retry might succeed when no deferred bits exist, accounting for start offset and wrap choice, or atomically moves deferred bits into the free state and reports progress.
Busy count equals set bits minus deferred bits, and liveness test ignores deferred bits.

Wake batch stays within fixed lower and upper bounds derived from effective depth divided among wait queues, with updates applied only on change and a per user variant dividing depth before the same bounding.

Hash table mutation serializes lookup plus insertion under a per bucket guard, walker roster changes serialize under a table wide spin guard, read side sections protect insertion retries and walk scans, a mutex guards lifetime operations, and a read barrier orders observation of successor tables.

Bitmap word reclamation serializes under a per word interrupt saving spin guard, bit claims use atomic test and set with atomic clearing of deferred masks, depth and wake values use single access ordering primitives, and hints use cpu local access.

Iterator state comprises owning table reference, current slot and skip offset, saved node and list positions, end marker, and roster linkage to the table being scanned, with list mode tracking both node and inner list element.

Hash table state includes parameters and key length, element counter and limit, current table reference, list mode flag, table wide lock and mutex, and deferred work items, while bucket tables carry size, nesting depth, walker roster, successor link, and reclamation callback.

Bitmap state holds depth, granularity shift, word count, round robin flag, per cpu hints, and word array; each word holds live bits, deferred bits, and a guard; queue state adds shallow limit, wake batch, lifecycle counters, and wait channels.
Insertion loops over protected attempt, locked lookup and insert, accounting and growth check, repeating while a new table is produced and converting lingering contention into a rehash result.

Walking moves from unregistered to registered idle, to protected scanning with position validation, across slots and successor tables with restart signaling, to terminal end state, with stop returning to registered idle unless reclamation detaches the reference.

Bit allocation maps a hint to a starting word, scans for a clear bit with optional wrap, invokes deferred reclamation on failure and retries, then steps through remaining words from the start with wrapping until success or exhaustion.

Concurrent resize can attach successor tables and relocate entries, so successor and walk paths revalidate saved positions, treat vanished predecessors as missing, follow successor links only after ordering, and avoid rejoining tables already scheduled for reclamation.

Allocation without hints, full maps, and depth changes need care: missing hints warn and fail, exhaustion returns a negative marker and resets hints, resize flushes deferred state first, and diagnostic dumps snapshot words to avoid tearing.

Initialization validates configuration and handles allocation failure by releasing partial state and retrying the smallest size with unfailing semantics for the hash table, or reporting memory exhaustion for bitmap and queue setup.

Insertion reports transient retry EAGAIN and duplicate EEXIST, successor lookup reports missing ENOENT and unsupported EOPNOTSUPP for list mode, configuration checks report invalid EINVAL, and setup paths report memory exhaustion ENOMEM.

Sizing uses defaults HASH_DEFAULT_SIZE and HASH_MIN_SIZE with word width BITS_PER_LONG, fanout derived from PAGE_SHIFT, queue tuning from SBQ_WAIT_QUEUES bounded by SBQ_WAKE_BATCH, full depth sentinel UINT_MAX, element cap at two to thirty one, hint inflation by four thirds, growth threshold at seventy five percent, and diagnostic rows of sixteen bytes.
Deferred maintenance is armed during initialization as both process context work and interrupt context work, with growth beyond threshold queueing the interrupt variant from insertion context.
